newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate drops to 11.2 from 12.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate drops to 11.2 from 12.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate dropped to 11.2 from 12.3 percent on Monday amid abundant supply, which dealers ascribed to the latest one-percent cut in central bank's mandatory reserve ratio.
Daily settlements totalled 57.8 million kuna, against 103 million kuna on offer. But one bank that sought a two-month loan found no lenders.
Half of the traded volume consisted of fresh deals, mostly call money. Its weighted rate was reduced to 10.4 percent as one foreign bank granted a single 9.0 percent loan.
Insurers charged a steady 9.0 percent for old one-week and 12 percent for two-week funds.
One-week interbank loans were extended at rates ranging between 11 and 13 percent, and one-month loans between 15.5 and 18 percent.
The central bank's kuna midrates for Tuesday firmed to 6.1313 aginst the dollar and to 3.5647 versus the mark. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385 1 4557075
